<!-- generated by rfcspec-docs, do not edit -->

Checked against v0.2.0 on 2026-11-06: 7 shipped, 6 decided, 7 planned. **Shipped** exists in v0.2.0 and names the gate step (`task <name>`) or the test that holds it; **decided** is a decision in the design; **planned** is a milestone of the design's section 14, or what remains of one, and nothing more.

| Area | Capability | Status | What it means | Held by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read | [Plain text and RFCXML](/docs/concepts/catalogue) | shipped | Fetch and lock an RFC's plain text or RFCXML v3 source, read it into one document model, and extract its BCP 14 requirements with cited spans; RFC 9220 is the RFCXML test case. | `crates/rfcspec-cli/tests/rfcxml.rs` |
| Read | [The whole RFC index](/docs/catalog/rfcs) | shipped | Every RFC the index publishes as RFCXML or plain text, with its requirement counts by level and section and its RFCXML references, unreviewed. | `task bulk` |
| Profiles | [Four profiles end to end](/docs/catalog) | shipped | RFC 868, RFC 6455, RFC 1035 and RFC 5905: a reviewed overlay, lowered models that pass bounded exploration, and a generated codec crate with its tests. | `task time`, `task websocket`, `task dns`, `task ntp` |
| Profiles | [Recorded proposals and review](/docs/concepts/ai-proposals) | shipped | Status proposals from a model, recorded with their cited spans, settled by review into the overlay and replayed offline in the gate. | `task websocket` |
| Site | [The RFC explorer](/docs/catalog/rfcs) | shipped | Search and filter the RFC index, open an RFC's requirements by section, update graph and references, and see a profiled RFC's reviewed layer. | `task explorer` |
| Wire | [ABNF parse, resolve and match](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | shipped | RFC 5234 and RFC 7405 ABNF parsed, references resolved to rules, core rules and RFC imports, and input matched against a rule. | `crates/rfcspec-abnf/tests/rfc6455_core.rs` |
| Wire | [Catalogue grammars](/docs/concepts/catalogue) | shipped | Each section's ABNF figures collected into one catalogue grammar, from plain text and RFCXML. | `crates/rfcspec-wire/tests/grammars.rs` |
| Design | [The catalogue, rfcspec/1](/docs/concepts/catalogue) | decided | An RFC becomes requirements, grammars, layouts, registries, defined procedures and limits, each with a source span and a digest (design D1). | - |
| Design | [ESS as the target](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | decided | Machines lower to ess-protospec/1, message and value types and registries to an ess/N system; what ESS cannot carry is listed as a gap (design D2). | - |
| Design | [A wire-format sidecar](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | decided | Bytes and bits live in rfcspec-wire/1: ABNF verbatim, bit-level ABNF and packet layouts (design D3). | - |
| Design | [Communication semantics](/docs/concepts/communication-semantics) | decided | One value per axis for each protocol layer: unit, delivery, direction, multiplexing, exchange, correlation, lifetime, layering, roles (design D4). | - |
| Design | [AI proposes, review decides](/docs/concepts/ai-proposals) | decided | Model output is a recorded proposal with cited spans, replayed offline; no gate calls a model (design D5, D6). | - |
| Design | [Which kinds of RFC are modelled](/docs/concepts/rfc-kinds) | decided | Wire protocols, data formats, extensions and registries are modelled; algorithms as signatures with test vectors; the rest get a requirement catalogue (design D11). | - |
| M0 Read | [Defined terms and a survey by kind](/docs/design) | planned | What remains of M0: defined terms in the catalogue, and a survey classifying every RFC in the index by kind. | - |
| M1 Wire | [The rest of the wire layer](/docs/examples/websocket) | planned | What remains of M1: the RFC 2616 and bit-level ABNF dialects, packet diagrams read into layouts, the RFC 6455 frame agreement check, and the handshake codec and frame codec vectors. | - |
| M2 Lower | [Proposals for parties, semantics and machines](/docs/concepts/ai-proposals) | planned | What remains of M2: recorded proposals for the parties, the communication semantics and the WebSocket machines; status proposals, review and lowering are shipped. | - |
| M3 Generate | [A generated WebSocket core](/docs/examples/websocket) | planned | What remains of M3: machine, limits and roles in the generated crate, an Autobahn run and a recorded requirement matrix; the frame codec is shipped. | - |
| M4 DNS | [Concurrent DNS sessions and the gap proposals](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | planned | What remains of M4: concurrent sessions, and the ESS gap proposals G1, G3 and G4 with WebSocket and DNS as evidence; the header codec and query machine are shipped. | - |
| M5 Spindle | [RFCspec cores in Spindle](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | planned | The WebSocket codec as a pure WASM module and a websocket channel port in a Spindle environment. | - |
| M6 TCP | [A transport](/docs/concepts/communication-semantics) | planned | TCP as the hard case: sequence-number arithmetic, windows and timers from measurements. | - |
